text_to_speech: Where did you first hear about DiEM25 and what was your first thought? I heard about DiEM the first time when I went to a lecture by Srećko Horvat in our university, which was the first time in my university career that someone actually talked about politics in the university and he talked about European politics and really nailed it, so I thought what is behind this, what stands behind it? Although he only mentioned DiEM in a small sentence, I did some research and I kind of followed DiEM from there on. If you were president of the world for one day what would be the first thing that you would do? If I were president for a day, I would get rid of debt, so that everyone could start afresh, and build a more just world, in which everyone had the same opportunities. If I were president of the world for one day, I would paint all the buildings in very bright colours, so that we had one less reason to be pessimistic. Wow, that is a very difficult question, because in one day I don't think you can achieve that much, but, I would try to contact all the other world leaders, to get them together, to come to some agreement on how to proceed with the most urgent matters, being finance and social matters. What is your story with DiEM25? My meeting with DiEM25 is an amusing story, because I had a serious illness for a long time and I had plenty of time to surf the Internet and enlighten myself intellectually and politically, and for a long time I'd had the idea that nothing can be fixed at a national level, but only at a European level, and in fact DiEM25 was a bit like a revelation for me of this idea that we should unite to construct a Europe and resolve problems which will never be resolved at national level, and that's really the key idea that made me join DiEM25 and take on responsibility in the movement. In which language do you speak, in which language do you read, and in which do you dream? I speak multiple languages: English, my mother tongue Malayalam, hindi, and a little bit of broken Tamil. I dream in English and Malayalam, but  mostly in English now that I am living in Amsterdam. I read in English, Greek, Italian, Spanish and French, I speak all of them as well, but I dream in Spanish. What is the topic in world politics that interests you the most? I am very interested in the international development of the European countries. I believe that it is very necessary to create a real union between the European citizens to deal with the current problems. What are the qualities you appreciate most in a person? What I appreciate in a person is that they speak frankly, that they say what they really think, their competence, of course,  their human quality, their humanism, their ability to see things on a large scale,  rather than a narrow one. Which book left the biggest impression on you, and why would you recommend it to fellow DiEMers? 1984 by George Orwell, because, if you haven't read it, then you have to, it's a classic. It shows a frightening vision of the future, that should never become a reality, but at the same time is becoming a reality. And we must act against that. Know your enemy and so on. Why are you interested in DiEM Voice? I'm interested in DiEM Voice because I think it's important to use art to communicate, to show transparency, to share,  and above all, everything that is happening in DiEM I think is really important, and art can allow us to participate in that. What is the most frequently used word in politics today? The most frequently used word in politics today is "them". How do you practice solidarity? I work with various citizens' movements, specifically, I work with refugees, I give French courses to refugees, when they need it, I host them at my house, while they are waiting to get their paperwork. When you look at the world today, in which colour do you see it, and if you were to paint it, which colour would you use? My job is to create as much trouble as I can for the powers that be, and for the nationalist international, which is a grave concern for all us democrats. My favourite colour was always red, but the reason I think the DiEM colours are spectacular is because they blend the deep orange of progressive liberals with the red of the Marxist tradition into what we now need to do in Europe, which is to combine the forces of democrats that are both of a Marxist predisposition and a liberal one to stem the tide that is pushing us into circumstances that are inimicable to the interests of civilisation.
